observations: StudyRenderEngine.render checks actual Task.isCancelled OR the additional cancellation source at entry, immediately before cache promotion, after CPU/Metal work, and after backend validation. Retain is reached only after successful rendering and the final cooperative cancellation check, with no suspension before admission/return. Throwing render paths do not retain a result.

The actor serializes render requests. Cancellation during Metal validation propagates without selecting a failed backend; GPU work already submitted completes before its result is discarded. No concrete stale cache/publication defect was found.

ReferenceStudyPreview derives .task(id:) from the scene/subject request only while scenePhase is active. An inactive phase changes the identity to nil; scene/subject changes replace the task. Disappearance cancellation is delegated to SwiftUI .task lifetime rather than an explicit onDisappear callback. Post-await and post-image-conversion checks guard success publication, and cancellation errors are suppressed on the failure path.

Displayed frames carry their request identity. A prior same-subject successful image is explicitly marked Previous render/Updating; another subject and old errors are hidden. This intentional prior-frame presentation is distinct from publishing a cancelled result.

Native source includes deterministic entry/pre-cache cancellation, actual already-cancelled Task rejection, interrupted CPU rendering, final post-render cancellation followed by a cold-cache proof, invalid metadata rejection, and restoration of the original completed frame. These are reviewed test definitions, not executed outcomes.
